text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.
- The reduction of four escudos in the price of diesel oil for agriculture divides the Agriculture and Finance Ministries.
- Insurance company Real Seguros in difficulties. Insurance Institute of Portugal decided to intervene, obliging the company to maintain solvency levels.
- The government will provide a five billion escudos injection of funds to struggling wine company Casa do Douro.
- A European Union directive demands a reduction in the quantity of lead in tap water. The measure will cost 200 billion escudos and affect 90,000 dwellings.

- Tax proposals of the right-wing Popular Party (PP), which have been accepted by the government, will cost 5.5 billion escudos in 1997 and between 20 and 25 billion escudos in 1998, Under-Secretary for Tax Matters Antonio Carlos Santos told the paper.

- European Commission President Jacques Santer wrote to Prime Minister Antonio Guterres to say he supports conditions set by EU commissioner Monica Wulf-Mathies to approve 57 billion escudos in financing for the construction of Alqueva dam.
- Planning Minister Joao Cravinho will open an inquiry into the causes of yesterday's accident in the future Olivais underground station in Lisbon.

- Economy Minister Augusto Mateus does not exclude any of the three candidates bidding to buy tobacco company Tabaqueira, but has doubts over the distribution end of the bid by Philip Morris/Jorge de Mello, sources involved in the process said.
